Transport & itineraries · Ellora Cave 16

Kailasa Temple Half-Day Itinerary

A half day allows Cave 16 in depth plus a small selection of the ensemble. ASI suggests that 3–4 hours can prioritise Caves 10, 16, 21, 32 and 34, subject to what is open.

Google Maps ↗ ASI source listing ↗

Independent guide · Page reviewed 9 November 2026 · ASI listing consulted 2026-10-29

Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) is one monument within the UNESCO-listed Ellora Caves. Prices, opening status and routes are dated listings to re-check, not live confirmations.

Use ASI’s priority list as a ceiling, not a promise

ASI’s suggestion of Caves 10, 16, 21, 32 and 34 in a 3–4 hour visit is a useful historical and artistic spread: a Buddhist chaitya, the great monolithic temple, Brahmanical caves and a Jain group. It is a reference for planning, not a guarantee that every cave is open or reachable.

Confirm current closures with ASI, then drop stops rather than compressing the monument that brought you here.

A workable order

Start with admission and the route to Cave 16 while energy and light are good. Give the courtyard, upper facades and the Ravana panel proper time, then add one or two contrasting caves. Finish with the return walk and the agreed pick-up.

Allow separately for admission, internal walking, rests and any closed paths. Reviewed 9 November 2026.

When to scale back

Heat, monsoon surfaces, family pace or accessibility needs all argue for fewer caves. A shorter Cave 16-focused plan is on the one-hour page; a full ensemble day is on the Ellora one-day itinerary page.

Suggested order

  1. Confirm the day’s open caves with ASI
  2. Admission and walk to Cave 16
  3. Kailasa Temple: courtyard, upper facades, sculptural panels
  4. Vishvakarma Cave (Cave 10) as a Buddhist contrast
  5. One further cave from the ASI priority list, if open
  6. Return walk to the agreed pick-up point

An order of attention, not a timed guarantee. Closed areas, conservation work and your own pace take priority.

Frequently asked questions

Which caves does ASI suggest for a 3–4 hour visit?

ASI suggests Caves 10, 16, 21, 32 and 34 as a priority selection for a 3–4 hour visit. Confirm current access on site.

Can I see all 34 caves in half a day?

No. The property is extensive and ASI describes the scarp as nearly 2 km long. A short, deliberate selection is more realistic.

Should I add a guide?

That is a separate arrangement; see the guided tours page for the questions to ask before booking.
